study_identification.title: Mapping the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD using a framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization

study_characteristics.study_objective: To quantitatively estimate the neuroanatomical heterogeneity of OCD from a dimensional perspective by proposing a framework integrating normative model and non-negative matrix factorization (NMF).

dataset_name.answer: First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University dataset

quality_checking_detail.answer: The Image Quality Rating (IQR) combing image noise contrast ratio, inhomogeneity contrast ratio and root mean square was recorded to assess images quality.

predictor_effects.answer: Age and sex are modeled as fixed effects.

nm_vldtn_handle_ns.reason: The study is single-site, so no site effects are expected. They model age and sex. GPR can model non-linearity in age. However, they do not explicitly discuss other potential nuisance variables.
nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: we trained a Gaussian process regression model to predict voxel-wise GMV from age and sex in HCs

nm_vldtn_same_domain_nonindep.reason: The paper does not report validation metrics like explained variance on the training set.

nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.reason: The paper uses leave-one-out cross validation (LOOCV) to show that the framework can infer factor compositions of unseen patients. This is a form of independent validation within the same domain.
nm_vldtn_same_domain_indep.supporting_text: To examine the extendibility of our framework, we investigated whether the identified disease factors could be used to infer factor compositions of unseen patients using leave-one-out cross validation (LOOCV).

nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The paper does not use a different domain dataset for validation.

clinical_dataset.answer: First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University dataset

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: The Pearson's correlation coefficients between factor compositions and clinical characteristics including illness duration, age of onset and symptom severity were calculated. We also investigate whether there were significant differences between female and male patients in terms of factor compositions using two sample t-test.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: The proposed framework quantitatively estimating neuroanatomical heterogeneity paves the way for precision medicine in OCD.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: The study identified 4 robust latent disease factors in OCD. These factors correlated with clinical characteristics (illness duration, age of onset, symptom severity, and sex) and could distinguish two subtypes with opposite neuroanatomical differences compared with HCs. The framework also reconciled group-level and individual-level findings by showing that group-level differences could be derived from the identified factors.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: First, the sample size was modest. Second, we only included first-episode treatment-naive patients. Third, alcohol and tobacco were not controlled, and future studies should examine their effects on the latent disease factors. Fourth, we did not record the obsessive dimensions.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: The framework showed potential translational foreground as it could infer factor compositions of unseen patients.
